subject: environmental-science
title: Food Chains & Webs: Changes & Impacts
welcome_lead: When one species changes, ripples spread through the whole web.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: predator-prey, invasive species, balance.
final_note: Nature finds balance — until something major breaks the rules.

concepts.def: Number of one species in an area.

walkthroughs.body_html: If prey numbers rise, predators have more food and multiply. Then prey drops, predators starve and drop. The cycle wobbles toward balance.
A keystone species holds a community together. Wolves returning to Yellowstone changed deer behaviour and even how rivers flowed.
Invasive species (like grey squirrels in the UK) can out-compete native species and cause population crashes.

options: A species crucial to its community

mcqs.q: What does the 'tragedy of the commons' describe?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
It is a play about poor people.
Shared resources tend to be overexploited because individuals benefit personally while sharing costs.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils often nutrient-poor despite abundant vegetation?
options: Rainforests are deserts most of the year.
Rapid decomposition and uptake mean nutrients cycle quickly through living biomass, not soil.
Rainforests have rich soils because they are productive.
Because they generate too much energy.
